reason: E1 shows that W addition to a TiZrWMo HEA forms Mo-W-rich BCC precipitates and improves dynamic compressive strength, but it does not provide evidence for improved strain hardening, uniform elongation, delayed localization, or the Orowan bowing mechanism. The cited evidence supports only the general concept of precipitate strengthening under dynamic loading, leaving most key premises unsupported.
premises: Tungsten addition to a refractory HEA can form fine, uniformly dispersed W-rich precipitates in a BCC matrix.
Such precipitates strengthen strain hardening and delay localization under dynamic loading.
The strengthening mechanism is Orowan bowing of dislocations around precipitates.
This mechanism increases stored dislocation density and promotes uniform plastic deformation.
The predicted outcome (higher dynamic strength, improved uniform elongation, delayed localization) is achievable in a similar refractory HEA system.
